src/business/services/OrderService.ts: `placeOrderFromRequest(request: Request): Order` takes an Express request object.

src/business/services/OrderService.ts: `this.placeOrder(String(request.body['customerId']), (request.body['items'] as OrderItem[] | undefined) ?? [])` reads and converts values from the HTTP request body, which is presentation-layer work.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The file sits in the business (domain) layer and is described as a Fowler Service Layer. Most of it fits that role. placeOrder, cancelOrder and getOrder coordinate domain objects (Product.reserve, Order.cancel, PricingPolicy.discountFor, Money). They also call injected gateways the way a service layer is expected to. Which layers it imports from is out of scope for this check.

One method does not fit: placeOrderFromRequest(request: Request) takes an Express HTTP Request and reads and converts values from request.body. It pulls out 'customerId', turns it into a string, casts 'items' to OrderItem[] and defaults it to an empty array. Turning an HTTP request into use-case inputs is transport work. It belongs in the presentation layer, here OrderController, and not in a domain service. Because of this method the file fails the rubric.
